kestred opened issue #15262:

.clif Test Case

A loop that calls a function and keeps three f64 values live across the call: the call's argument v0, the factor
v1 and the running sum v6. The function has no vector value.

function %f(f64, f64, i64) -> f64 {
    sig0 = (f64) -> f64
    fn0 = %g sig0

block0(v0: f64, v1: f64, v2: i64):
    v3 = iconst.i64 0
    v4 = f64const 0.0
    v12 = iconst.i64 1
    jump block1(v3, v4)

block1(v5: i64, v6: f64):
    v7 = call fn0(v0)
    v8 = fmul v7, v1
    v9 = fadd v6, v8
    v10 = iadd v5, v12
    v11 = icmp ult v10, v2
    brif v11, block1(v10, v9), block2

block2:
    return v9
}

test run
target aarch64

; Writes whole q registers under high pressure, so that it uses v8 - v15 and,
; as AAPCS lets it, returns with only their low halves restored.
function %clobber_vectors(f64) -> f64 {
block0(v0: f64):
    v1 = splat.f64x2 v0

; No vector: the scalars stay in v8 - v15 across the call.
function %scalar_caller(f64, f64, f64) -> f64 {
    fn0 = colocated %clobber_vectors(f64) -> f64

block0(v0: f64, v1: f64, v2: f64):
    v3 = call fn0(v0)
    v4 = fmul v1, v2
    v5 = fadd v4, v1
    v6 = fadd v5, v2
    return v6
}
; run: %scalar_caller(0x1.0, 0x3.0, 0x5.0) == 0x17.0

; A vector live across the call: v8 - v15 stay clobbered, so it is spilled.
function %vector_caller(f64, f64) -> f64 {
    fn0 = colocated %clobber_vectors(f64) -> f64

block0(v0: f64, v1: f64):
    v2 = splat.f64x2 v1
    v3 = call fn0(v0)
    v4 = extractlane v2, 1
    v5 = fadd v4, v1
    return v5

Steps to Reproduce

  • First, build clif-util from wasmtime v50.0.0, the release that ships cranelift-codegen 0.137.0:
    curl -L https://github.com/bytecodealliance/wasmtime/archive/refs/tags/v50.0.0.tar.gz | tar xz cd wasmtime-50.0.0 cargo build --release -p cranelift-tools --bin clif-util

  • Then, compile the test case and print its disassembly:
    target/release/clif-util compile --target aarch64 --set opt_level=speed -D 1-test.clif
    clif-util compile only compiles, so the output does not depend on the host. The listings below omit the
    instruction bytes.

  • Then, apply the patch under Extra Info, build again, and compile the test case again.

Expected Results

The loop keeps v0, v1 and v6 in v8–v15 across the call, with no load or store per iteration. AAPCS64 preserves
the low 64 bits of those registers, which is all of an f64, and the prologue saves the ones that the function
uses. With the patch, the loop from 0x2c to 0x70 moves the values between registers, and the prologue saves d8,
d9 and d15 once:

Disassembly of 136 bytes <%f>:

4:  mov x29, sp
8:  stp x19, x20, [sp, #-0x10]!
c:  str d15, [sp, #-0x10]!

14:  mov    x20, x0

1c:  mov    v15.16b, v1.16b

24:  movi   v0.2s, #0
28:  mov    v9.16b, v0.16b
2c:  ldr    x13, #0x34

3c:  mov    v0.16b, v8.16b
40:  blr    x13
44:  add    x19, x19, #1
48:  mov    v1.16b, v15.16b
4c:  fmul   d16, d0, d1
50:  mov    v0.16b, v9.16b
54:  fadd   d0, d0, d16
58:  mov    x0, x20
5c:  cmp    x19, x0
60:  b.hs   #0x74
64:  mov    x20, x0
68:  mov    v9.16b, v0.16b
6c:  mov    v15.16b, v1.16b
70:  b  #0x2c
74:  ldp    d8, d9, [sp], #0x10
78:  ldr    d15, [sp], #0x10
7c:  ldp    x19, x20, [sp], #0x10
80:  ldp    x29, x30, [sp], #0x10
84:  ret

Actual Results

Every iteration stores and reloads the floats: the loop from 0x28 to 0x6c has three 128-bit loads (ldur q) and
two 128-bit stores (stur q), to keep values that the callee would have preserved:

4:  mov x29, sp

Versions and Environment

Cranelift version or commit: cranelift-codegen 0.137.0, with regalloc2 0.15.2, built into clif-util from wasmtime
v50.0.0 (commit ebe5e8df1f4e12c5fc2f5954926881d8d61367d8) with rustc 1.98.0, --release and default features.

Operating system: macOS 26.6.2 (build 25G83).

Architecture: arm64 (Apple M5 Pro), compiling for --target aarch64.

Extra Info

The limitation. default_aapcs_clobbers() in isa/aarch64/abi.rs says:

The upper 64 bits of v8 - v15 inclusive are also caller-saves. However, because we cannot currently represent
partial registers to regalloc2, we indicate here that every vector register is caller-save. Because this function
is used at callsites, approximating in this direction (save more than necessary) is conservative and thus safe.

This stopgap was chosen in #2254 and #2267, where a follow-up was noted so that prologues and epilogues deal only with
the lower 64 bits. In regalloc2, partial registers are out of scope (bytecodealliance/regalloc2#247).

The proposal. A function with no value wider than 64 bits loses nothing when a call clobbers only the upper
halves of v8–v15, so it can drop them from that call's clobbers without regalloc2 knowing about partial registers:

  • A new provided method, ABIMachineSpec::get_regs_partially_clobbered_by_call(callee_conv, is_exception), returns
    v8–v15 on aarch64 wherever the default AAPCS clobbers apply, and an empty set elsewhere and on other targets.

  • Callee::new computes a has_wide_values flag from the types of the function's dfg values, as it already scans
    the dynamic types. A type that the backend cannot place in registers counts as wide.

  • When the function has no wide value, gen_call_info drops partial(callee_conv) ∩ partial(caller_conv) from the
    call's clobbers.

There is no new setting and no call for the embedder to make. The other users of the static clobber sets are
unchanged and stay conservative. s390x carries the same comment and could opt in the same way.

Soundness.

  • The intersection with the caller's own convention matters for a PreserveAll caller. A call's clobbers also decide
    what the prologue saves, so such a caller still treats v8–v15 as clobbered and saves all 128 bits of them.

  • An exception edge is narrowed only where the unwinder already restores callee-saves, that is, for a SystemV or
    Apple try_call.

  • Winch, PreserveAll and Tail exception edges are unchanged.

Evidence. With the patch, two aarch64 filetests change when blessed: in call.clif and user_stack_maps.clif,
the q-register spills become mov to v8–v15, and the prologue saves d8, d11, d12 or d15 with stp or
str. Stock clif-util fails both blessed files. With the patch and the blessed files,

target/release/clif-util test cranelift/filetests/filetests

printed 1322 tests with no failure. A runtime test, 1-run.clif beside this issue, calls a function that writes
all 128 bits of v8–v15 from a caller that keeps scalars in them across the call:

target/release/clif-util test 1-run.clif

It printed 1 tests with no failure, with and without the patch. With its expected value changed from 0x17.0 to
0x18.0, it failed with actual: 0x1.7000000000000p4, which shows that the test runs.

A precise alternative would be per-value partial clobbers in regalloc2.

+++ b/cranelift/codegen/src/isa/aarch64/abi.rs
@@ -1210,6 +1210,20 @@ impl ABIMachineSpec for AArch64MachineDeps {

+        is_exception: bool,

kestred edited issue #15262:

.clif Test Case

A loop that calls a function and keeps three f64 values live across the call: the call's argument v0, the factor
v1 and the running sum v6. The function has no vector value.

test.clif

function %f(f64, f64, i64) -> f64 {
    sig0 = (f64) -> f64
    fn0 = %g sig0

block0(v0: f64, v1: f64, v2: i64):
    v3 = iconst.i64 0
    v4 = f64const 0.0
    v12 = iconst.i64 1
    jump block1(v3, v4)

block1(v5: i64, v6: f64):
    v7 = call fn0(v0)
    v8 = fmul v7, v1
    v9 = fadd v6, v8
    v10 = iadd v5, v12
    v11 = icmp ult v10, v2
    brif v11, block1(v10, v9), block2

block2:
    return v9
}

Steps to Reproduce

  • First, build clif-util from wasmtime v50.0.0, the release that ships cranelift-codegen 0.137.0:
    curl -L https://github.com/bytecodealliance/wasmtime/archive/refs/tags/v50.0.0.tar.gz | tar xz cd wasmtime-50.0.0 cargo build --release -p cranelift-tools --bin clif-util

  • Then, compile the test case and print its disassembly:
    target/release/clif-util compile --target aarch64 --set opt_level=speed -D 1-test.clif
    clif-util compile only compiles, so the output does not depend on the host. The listings below omit the
    instruction bytes.

  • Then, apply the patch under Extra Info, build again, and compile the test case again.

Extra Info

The limitation. default_aapcs_clobbers() in isa/aarch64/abi.rs says:

The upper 64 bits of v8 - v15 inclusive are also caller-saves. However, because we cannot currently represent
partial registers to regalloc2, we indicate here that every vector register is caller-save. Because this function
is used at callsites, approximating in this direction (save more than necessary) is conservative and thus safe.

This stopgap was chosen in #2254 and #2267, where a follow-up was noted so that prologues and epilogues deal only with
the lower 64 bits. In regalloc2, partial registers are out of scope (bytecodealliance/regalloc2#247).

The proposal. A function with no value wider than 64 bits loses nothing when a call clobbers only the upper
halves of v8–v15, so it can drop them from that call's clobbers without regalloc2 knowing about partial registers:

  • A new provided method, ABIMachineSpec::get_regs_partially_clobbered_by_call(callee_conv, is_exception), returns
    v8–v15 on aarch64 wherever the default AAPCS clobbers apply, and an empty set elsewhere and on other targets.

  • Callee::new computes a has_wide_values flag from the types of the function's dfg values, as it already scans
    the dynamic types. A type that the backend cannot place in registers counts as wide.

  • When the function has no wide value, gen_call_info drops partial(callee_conv) ∩ partial(caller_conv) from the
    call's clobbers.

There is no new setting and no call for the embedder to make. The other users of the static clobber sets are
unchanged and stay conservative. s390x carries the same comment and could opt in the same way.

Soundness.

  • The intersection with the caller's own convention matters for a PreserveAll caller. A call's clobbers also decide
    what the prologue saves, so such a caller still treats v8–v15 as clobbered and saves all 128 bits of them.

  • An exception edge is narrowed only where the unwinder already restores callee-saves, that is, for a SystemV or
    Apple try_call.

  • Winch, PreserveAll and Tail exception edges are unchanged.

Evidence. With the patch, two aarch64 filetests change when blessed: in call.clif and user_stack_maps.clif,
the q-register spills become mov to v8–v15, and the prologue saves d8, d11, d12 or d15 with stp or
str. Stock clif-util fails both blessed files. With the patch and the blessed files,
